channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: Quem tem razão na disputa política sobre o tarifaço, segundo pesquisa
item.description: The Nexus/BTG poll shows 41% of Brazilians agree with Lula’s view that Flávio Bolsonaro pushed the U.S. to impose tariffs to harm his reelection bid, while another 41% side with Flávio, blaming Lula for poor diplomatic relations with the Trump administration. 52% believe the tariff is politically motivated, not economic, highlighting Brazil’s deep electoral polarization.

item.title: ‘Aprendi muito com os meus erros’, diz José Dirceu em sua volta ao cenário eleitoral
item.description: José Dirceu said he learned from his political mistakes and advocates for the PT's renewal with new leaders like Fernando Haddad, while maintaining a long-term national project. He believes Lula should present a government program with clear goals for the next four years, focusing on violence, education, and well-paid job creation. Dirceu emphasized the need for party reform, political consensus, and South American integration to drive a deep transformation in Brazil over the coming decade.

item.title: Zema defende 'privatizar tudo', reforma previdenciária e revisão de programas sociais
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential candidate for the Novo party, reiterated his proposal to privatize all Brazilian state-owned enterprises, stating that none are immune to divestment. He also advocated for a pension reform and a review of social programs, aligning with the party's liberal agenda.

item.title: TSE amplia cooperação com plataformas digitais para combater a desinformação nas Eleições 2026
item.description: The TSE signed memoranda of understanding with Meta, X, Telegram, TikTok, Kwai, LinkedIn, and Google Brazil to combat disinformation in the 2026 elections. The agreements, effective until December 31, 2026, establish joint actions without financial transfers. The initiative aims to protect electoral integrity through platform-specific cooperation.

item.title: Zema lança candidatura com foco em segurança e economia, diz ser anti-PT e não critica Flávio
item.description: Romeu Zema launched his presidential candidacy for the Novo Party, positioning himself as anti-PT and focusing on public security, economic management, and anti-corruption. He avoided criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro despite distancing himself after the Master case revelations, and stated that his running mate remains undecided, with former STF minister Joaquim Barbosa under consideration.

item.title: Sem citar Trump, Cármen Lúcia defende democracia e diz que ninguém deve interferir no país
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia defended Brazilian democracy and non-foreign interference at an SBPC event in Rio de Janeiro, emphasizing that Brazilians must decide their own future. She reaffirmed the reliability of electronic voting machines and linked democratic struggle to resistance during the military dictatorship, citing the SBPC as a space for voice when freedoms were repressed.

item.title: Um alívio econômico para Lula na nova pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: The BTG Nexus poll shows improved perception of Brazil's economy, driven by slowing food inflation and a resilient labor market with low unemployment and real wage growth. This economic optimism correlates with a growing advantage for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the presidential race, according to economist Bruno Perri, who notes that household debt and high interest rates still constrain a broader confidence recovery despite positive indicators.

item.title: “Caricatura patética” e “puxa-saco de Trump”, diz Boulos sobre Milei
item.description: Chief of Staff of the Presidency of the Republic, Guilherme Boulos, harshly criticized Argentine President Javier Milei, calling him a 'pathetic caricature' and a 'Trump lackey'. The remarks followed Milei's characterization of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as a 'prisoner'.

item.title: Vereadora do Ceará pivô de crise entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Michelle ganha força para ser vice
item.description: Fortaleza city councilwoman Priscila Costa, an ally of Michelle Bolsonaro, is gaining support among allies to become the vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential ticket, which is moving toward a pure PL party slate. Her rise comes amid tensions between Bolsonarist factions aligned with Flávio and Michelle, with Priscila serving as a unifying figure and strengthening the electoral base in Ceará.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula e presidente da Coreia do Sul fazem declaração conjunta
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva received South Korean President Lee Jae-myung at the Palácio da Alvorada for a bilateral meeting, signing of agreements, and a joint press statement at 1:20 PM. The meeting strengthens the close ties between Brazil and South Korea following Lula's visit to Seoul in February 2026. The Alvorada reception is traditionally reserved for heads of state with whom Brazil maintains strategic relations.

item.title: Pesquisa: o maior obstáculo para Flávio no segundo turno, segundo cientista político
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula with 42% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 33% in the first round, with a technical tie in the second round (47% to 43%). Political scientist Leandro Consentino warns that the competitiveness of the runoff means Lula must aim to win in the first round, as Flávio remains the leading right-wing candidate due to the Bolsonaro family’s consolidated electoral base.

item.title: O efeito ‘duvidoso’ das falas de Javier Milei para a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The controversial statements by Argentine President Javier Milei during the convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy sparked a diplomatic crisis between Brazil and Argentina, including insults toward Lula and Alexandre de Moraes, prompting official rebukes from Itamaraty and Brazil's finance minister. According to editor José Benedito da Silva, Milei's support is unlikely to expand Flávio's voter base, as Milei's supporters already back Bolsonaro, and the rhetoric may instead alienate moderate voters.

item.title: Governo Lula insistirá em banir “jogo do tigrinho” antes das eleições
item.description: The Lula government plans to advance with the ban on the 'tigrinho game' and other betting platforms after the Congressional recess, starting in the first week of August, aiming to position the president as a defender of indebted families ahead of the 2026 elections. The measure adds to existing restrictions on betting advertising and blocks access to betting sites for beneficiaries of Bolsa Família and BPC, despite the sector collecting R$5.89 billion in taxes from January to May — an 85.9% increase from the same period in 2025. A bill by government leader in the Chamber, Paulo Pimenta, seeking to ban electronic or algorithm-based gambling games like digital slot machines and the 'tigrinho', has remained stalled since May.

item.title: MDB ‘foge’ de radicalização, libera alianças e foca em aumentar recursos
item.description: The MDB has decided not to launch a presidential candidate in 2026 or formally support any presidential contender in the first round, choosing federal neutrality to preserve its congressional influence and secure access to electoral fund resources. The strategy allows state directories to form local alliances based on convenience, as seen in São Paulo (supporting Tarcísio de Freitas), Rio de Janeiro (supporting Eduardo Paes), and Minas Gerais (nominating Gabriel Azevedo for a state candidacy). The party prioritizes allocating over R$ 400 million from the FEFC to strengthen its parliamentary caucuses.

item.title: Responsabilidade por tarifaço expõe divisão entre gerações no país, aponta pesquisa
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows a generational split on blame for U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods: voters aged 16–24 favor Flávio Bolsonaro (47% vs 42%), while those over 60 back Lula (44% vs 36%). Intermediate age groups show a technical tie or slight Bolsonaro lead, with the highest uncertainty among seniors.

item.title: Maioria vê tarifaço de Trump ao Brasil como tentativa de favorecer Flávio Bolsonaro, diz DataFolha
item.description: A DataFolha survey reveals that 52% of Brazilians believe the U.S. tariff increase on Brazilian products aims to favor Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential candidacy. This perception is strongest among Lula voters (73%), while only 37% disagree and 11% had no opinion. The survey also shows limited public awareness: 37% say they have no knowledge of the tariff hike, 34% are somewhat informed, and only 25% consider themselves well informed.

item.title: Zema critica PT e STF, diz conhecer 'Brasil real' e quer presídio na Amazônia para prender faccionados
item.description: Romeu Zema was officially nominated as the Novo Party's presidential candidate for 2026, without yet announcing a running mate. In his speech, he criticized the Lula government, the PT, and STF ministers, claiming to be the only candidate who knows the 'real Brazil'. He proposed classifying criminal factions as terrorist organizations and building a prison in the Amazon to detain organized crime leaders.

item.title: A arriscada aposta de Caiado e Kassab: atacar Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The PSD, led by Gilberto Kassab, broke with its tradition of neutrality by nominating Ronaldo Caiado as presidential candidate with Kassab as vice president, making a bold bet to challenge the centrão and compete for the presidency in 2026, despite Kassab’s history of serving in both left-wing and right-wing governments.

item.title: Zema é oficializado e diz que não terá “problema Master”
item.description: The Novo party officially nominated former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema as its presidential candidate during a national convention in Brasília. Zema emphasized that his campaign will not be burdened by the Banco Master scandal, stating there will be no 'Master problem' affecting his candidacy. He defended his record as governor as the foundation for his presidential bid.

item.title: Novo confirma candidatura de Zema à Presidência, mas adia anúncio de vice
item.description: The New Party officially confirmed former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema as its presidential candidate in a convention held in Brasília on Monday (27). However, the party has not yet decided on his running mate, postponing the announcement of the vice-presidential candidate. The complete ticket will be revealed at a later date.

item.title: Lula é desaprovado por 63% e aprovado por 30% no Acre, diz pesquisa
item.description: In Acre, 63% of the population disapproves of President Lula's government, while 30% approve, according to a Real Time Big Data survey from July 2026. Performance evaluation shows 48% rate the government as 'bad' or 'terrible', 26% as 'regular', and 22% as 'good' or 'excellent'. The poll interviewed 1,600 people aged 16+ between July 22–25, with a 2-point margin of error.

item.title: Cavalaria e guarda de honra: veja como foi a recepção a Lee Jae-myung
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung was received with military honors at the Palácio da Alvorada on July 27, 2026, including an escort by the Dragões da Independência, a review of the honor guard, national anthems, and a meeting with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The ceremony followed standard protocol for receiving heads of state and featured an outdoor musical performance in the palace gardens.

item.title: Hana Ghassan e Dr. Daniel empatam no PA, diz Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released on July 27, 2026, shows Governor Hana Ghassan (MDB) and former mayor Dr. Daniel Santos (Podemos) tied in Pará, with 24% and 20% in the first first-round scenario and 25% and 23% in the second, all within a 3-point margin of error. In the runoff scenario, Ghassan leads with 36% to Santos’ 35%, with 18% undecided and 11% planning blank/null votes. The survey interviewed 900 voters from July 21–25, has a 95% confidence level, and is registered with the TSE under PA-04548/2026.

item.title: Vieira se reúne com embaixador da Argentina e repudia falas de Milei
item.description: The Brazilian government summoned Argentina's ambassador to Brazil, Daniel Raimondi, to convey its repudiation of statements made by Argentine President Javier Milei, who called Minister Alexandre de Moraes a 'bald trash' during a PL event in São Paulo. Brazil also recalled its own ambassador to Argentina, Júlio Bitelli, for consultations—a diplomatic move indicating greater seriousness. The developments followed Milei's participation in the PL convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy.

item.title: Novo oficializa candidatura de Romeu Zema sem indicação de vice
item.description: The Novo party officially launched Romeu Zema's presidential candidacy at a convention in Brasília on Monday, the 27th. Zema has not yet chosen a running mate, though former STF justice Joaquim Barbosa is being considered for the vice-presidential slot. Zema plans to meet with Barbosa soon. Novo president João Caldas said he does not oppose the pairing and called it a 'great ticket'.

item.title: PSB espera até 3ª feira definição de Josué sobre vice do PT em MG
item.description: The PSB expects to decide by Tuesday (July 28, 2026) whether Josué Gomes, former Fiesp president and son of José Alencar, will be the vice-presidential candidate on Patrus Ananias’s (PT) ticket for Minas Gerais governor. The decision hinges on internal discussions and potential direct involvement from Lula, who supports the alliance. The PSB also considers Jarbas Soares Júnior as an alternative for vice or Senate, maintaining the strategy of a majoritarian coalition with the PT.

item.title: MDB decide não apoiar nenhum candidato ao Planalto e libera diretórios estaduais para definir apoios
item.description: The MDB decided not to support any presidential candidate in the 2026 elections, allowing state directories to define their own alignments based on local realities amid strong political polarization. The move aims to prevent internal division, as the party shows regional differences — favoring Lula’s government in the Northeast and North, while resisting in the South, Southeast and Central-West. MDB national president Baleia Rossi stated that national liberation unifies the party and strengthens its state-level performance, with prospects of fielding its own candidate in 2030.

item.title: O show de Milei
item.description: Javier Milei's diatribes against Lula and Alexandre de Moraes are disproportionate and reveal the triumph of the Argentine president's ego over his country's interests. His irrational rhetoric makes rational analysis difficult and harms bilateral relations.

item.title: Tarcísio atrai siglas que apoiaram PSDB, triplica tempo de TV e terá 71% do horário eleitoral
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) has secured the support of all parties that backed Rodrigo Garcia in 2022, nearly tripling his electoral TV and radio time. He is projected to receive 70.8% of free electoral airtime — about 6 minutes and 23 seconds per 9-minute block — compared to Fernando Haddad’s (PT) 29.2%. This advantage stems from alliances with PL, PSD, União Progressista, MDB, Podemos, and federations like PRD-Solidariedade and PSDB-Cidadania, solidifying support from former Tucano rivals over the past four years.

item.title: Flávio tem 57% contra 34% de Lula no 2º turno no Acre, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data survey released on July 27, 2026, shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 57% against 34% for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in a hypothetical presidential runoff in Acre. In the first-round scenario, Flávio also leads with 50% versus Lula’s 30%. The poll surveyed 1,600 people from July 22–25, has a 2-point margin of error, and is registered with the TSE under BR-08086/2026.

item.title: Crusoé: Flávio ganha um trono, mas não um reino
item.description: The Liberal Party (PL) convention in São Paulo was designed to establish Flávio Bolsonaro’s hegemony within the bolsonarist movement, symbolically placing him center stage alongside his wife, Fernanda. Despite the institutional backing and visibility, the event did not secure him full control of the movement, revealing internal divisions and resistance from other bolsonarist leaders.

item.title: Maioria diz que família, amigos, imprensa e redes sociais não influenciam voto, aponta Datafolha
item.description: A majority of Brazilians state that the opinions of family, friends, journalists, social media influencers, and religious leaders will not influence their choice of presidential candidate in the 2026 elections, according to a Datafolha poll released on July 27, 2026.

item.title: Novo oficializa a candidatura de Romeu Zema à Presidência da República
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) officially launched his presidential candidacy at the party's national convention in Brasília, attended by party president Eduardo Ribeiro. Despite not yet announcing a running mate, Zema cited a BTG/Nexus poll showing him technically tied with Lula in a potential second-round runoff (42% to 46%). He positioned himself as a champion of right-wing economic liberalism, citing his Minas Gerais administration as a national model and mentioning Michelle Bolsonaro as a possible vice-presidential pick — which she has denied.

item.title: Durigan diz que próximo governo deve detalhar corte de gastos este ano
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that the next government, whether continuity or not, must present, still in 2026 after the elections, the details of a spending cut to begin in 2027, focused on mandatory expenditures. He emphasized the need for a fiscal adjustment of 2 percentage points of GDP on spending to bring public debt down, while advocating for greater efficiency and room for structural investments. Durigan also suggested that the STF act as a moderator of 'budget-bomb' proposals in Congress, which increase fixed spending without financing sources.

item.title: Lula recebe presidente sul-coreano para ampliar comércio
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung was received by Lula at the Palácio da Alvorada with full state honors, signaling a deepening of bilateral ties. The visit includes discussions on trade, technology, defense, and a potential Mercosul-South Korea free trade agreement, with emphasis on semiconductors, critical minerals, and energy transition.

item.title: Crise com Argentina: Embaixador chega a Brasília; conversa com Vieira ocorre até 4ª
item.description: Brazil's ambassador to Argentina, Julio Bitelli, returned to Brasília after being recalled by Itamaraty in protest over Argentine President Javier Milei's insults toward President Lula and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. Bitelli is expected to meet with Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira by Wednesday, though a detailed talk may be delayed due to Vieira's schedule, including a meeting with South Korea's president and a trip to Peru. Argentina's ambassador in Brazil was also summoned for explanations, worsening bilateral tensions that have persisted since Milei took office.

item.title: Zema chega à convenção sem vice e com candidatura pouco competitiva
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) was officially announced as the presidential candidate at a convention in Brasília, but without a running mate and limited support from major parties. He trails behind leaders Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro in voter intentions, and stated the vice-presidential pick will be decided later, possibly through an alliance with Podemos or a Novo-only ticket. Zema reiterated he will not be Bolsonaro’s running mate and will stay in the race until the end.

item.title: Sem vice, Novo confirma Zema à Presidência da República
item.description: The Novo Party officially nominated former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema as its presidential candidate at a national convention in Brasília, with no running mate yet named. Zema emphasized his private-sector background, criticized the Supreme Federal Court and the Lula government, claiming he possesses the credentials to win, while party president Eduardo Ribeiro praised Zema’s Minas Gerais administration as a model to defeat the PT nationally.

item.title: Ministro das Relações Exteriores se reúne com embaixador da Argentina e transmite repúdio sobre declarações de Milei sobre Lula
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met with Argentina's ambassador to Brazil, Daniel Raimondi, to convey the Brazilian government's repudiation of statements made by Argentine President Javier Milei during his visit to São Paulo, in which he attacked President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, democratic institutions, and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The Itamaraty deemed the remarks unprecedented and ordered the return of Brazil's ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations, escalating diplomatic tension following Milei's comments at the PL convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy.

item.title: Governador de Buenos Aires critica Milei por fala sobre governo do Brasil: ‘Vergonha alheia’
item.description: The governor of Buenos Aires, Axel Kicillof, criticized Argentine President Javier Milei's remarks during Brazil's PL national convention, calling them 'foreign shame' for insulting President Lula and the Brazilian government. Kicillof stated Milei does not represent the Argentine people's sentiment and defended regional integration, emphasizing Brazil as Argentina's main trading partner and warning that Milei's comments risk investments, exports, and jobs.

item.title: Zema oficializa candidatura ao Planalto nesta segunda e deixa vice para agosto
item.description: Romeu Zema officially announced his candidacy for President of Brazil during the Novo party’s national convention in Brasília. The vice-presidential pick remains undecided, with ongoing negotiations for political alliances, and Joaquim Barbosa is the primary target. His campaign platform emphasizes public security, privatizations, and criticism of Lula’s foreign policy.

item.title: Quais foram as declarações de Milei que abriram crise com o governo Lula
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei triggered a diplomatic crisis with Brazil after insulting President Lula, calling him a 'prisoner', 'thief', and 'socialist trash', and referring to Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes as 'bald trash', during a speech at the PL convention in São Paulo. The Brazilian government summoned Argentina’s ambassadors in Brasília and Buenos Aires for explanations, condemning the remarks as an unprecedented interference in Brazilian elections and an attack on the dignity of a head of state on their own soil.

item.title: Paraguai e Argentina podem ser entrave para aceleração de acordo entre Mercosul e China, diz especialista em economia chinesa
item.description: Despite a favorable geopolitical moment to accelerate a Mercosul-China agreement, Paraguay and Argentina pose significant obstacles, according to Chinese economy expert Roberto Dumas. Paraguay’s recognition of Taiwan as an independent country is identified as the primary barrier, given China’s sensitivity on the issue.

item.title: O candidato que se sai melhor contra Lula no segundo turno em nova pesquisa
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) performs best against Lula in a hypothetical second-round scenario, with 43% voting intention versus Lula’s 45%, within the poll’s two-point margin of error. Over two weeks, the gap between Lula and Caiado narrowed from nine to two points, showing the most significant shift among tested candidates. In the first round, Lula leads with 42%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 33%, while Caiado trails at 6%.

item.title: A força da marca Bolsonaro e a construção do mito Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro was confirmed as the PL candidate and remains in a runoff position according to Datafolha, despite investigations into the fate of over R$60 million donated by jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro. His campaign promises to implement Zero-Based Budgeting (OBZ), a private-sector management method linked to strict spending cuts. Meanwhile, Lula has retooled his campaign to retell his personal story, aiming to counter the perception among youth that he is 'part of the system', with Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola) serving as the link to the Planalto.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio diz que Bolsonaro não sabia de vídeo com IA exibido na convenção; especialistas apontam riscos jurídicos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign claims the AI-generated video shown at the PL national convention was produced exclusively by their team, without prior knowledge from Jair Bolsonaro, and complied with TSE rules and STF restrictions. The defense relies on the video's initial AI disclosure and its classification as an intraparty act. However, electoral law experts warn the case may be reviewed by electoral justice and could have implications in the STF.

item.title: ‘Interferência externa’: o apoio de Xi Jinping a Lula em meio a pressão de Trump
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed support for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in his opposition to external interference during a phone call amid U.S. tariff pressure under Donald Trump. Lula emphasized accelerating the Mercosul-China trade agreement and reaffirmed his commitment to market diversification, while Trump imposed new tariffs on Brazilian goods, which Lula characterizes as political interference in the election year.

item.title: Eleição será marcada por melhoras nas contas do País, afirma Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that Lula’s third term will end in 2026 with respect for institutions and improved fiscal indicators. He emphasized that the upcoming election will be marked by progress in public accounts, reflecting the effectiveness of current economic policies.

item.title: Governo Lula é aprovado por 47% e rejeitado por 49%, diz BTG/Nexus
item.description: Lula's government has 47% approval and 49% rejection, according to BTG/Nexus, with slight fluctuation from the previous survey. Approval reaches 62% in the Northeast, while disapproval hits 64% in the South. The margin of error is 2 percentage points.

item.title: China se opõe à interferência externa no Brasil, diz Xi Jinping a Lula
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping reaffirmed China's support for Brazilian sovereignty and opposition to external interference during a call with Lula, emphasizing cooperation in AI, satellites, critical minerals, and fertilizers. The statement comes amid tensions with the U.S., which Lula accused of attempting to discredit Brazil's elections by denying visas to American officials. Both countries also agreed to accelerate a Mercosul-China agreement with necessary flexibilities.
